name: @bananaworld/design-system
description: Shared Bananaworld design system + shared pure logic used by both Bananaworld-DC and Bananaworld-CRM. The UI barrel ('.') is the 28 pure UI primitives + per-surface (data-surface) tokens — pure presentation only: no network, no permission/scope logic (TECH-COMP-003 / ADR-001). A separate './pricing' subpath ships THE single shared price-calculation engine (pure, no IO — CRM ADR-007 / PRD-FUNC-060) so a quote and the eventual order price identically; it never imports the UI layer. Shipped as TypeScript source; consumers transpile it via Next.js transpilePackages.

pnpm.//overrides: nanoid — TWO high advisories (GHSA-28wg-ghj8-5hjv <3.3.16, GHSA-2v37-7h3g-55p8 <3.3.18; both are infinite-loop DoS on a nonsensical size, no disclosure) reach the prod closure by ONE path: the auto-installed `next` PEER > postcss@8.4.31 > nanoid@3.3.12. They were published after this repo was last touched, so they fail the Dependency Audit on EVERY pull request here, including one that changes nothing. OVERRIDDEN RATHER THAN IGNORED, deliberately: bananaworld-dc met the identical advisory first and resolved it this way (a20cf381, PR #160, 2026-08-08), and the standing next-peer ignore above records its own revisit trigger as "when the estate advisory batch bumps next" — which is this. An ignore here would book a 7th standing exception at the exact moment the 6th said to stop. ^3.3.17 resolves 3.3.18 and clears both. Owner CHOSE this over extending ignoreGhsas, in writing, at the CR-DESIGN-SYSTEM-002 decision gate on 2026-08-14 (D-12). No Hard Rule 2 citation belongs here and its absence is the point: an override trades nothing away, so unlike the ignores below it is a fix and not an exception. Verified by running: `pnpm audit --prod --audit-level=high` exits 1 without this and 0 with it; `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` passes, so the lock and manifest agree.
pnpm.//overrides-next-rce: next — TWO CRITICAL advisories published 2026-09-08 (GHSA-2xp9-vwfh-vxw4 unauthenticated RCE in the Image Optimization API on AVIF input; GHSA-p293-qw3h-jr36 unauthenticated RCE on windows-hosted servers, both <15.5.24) plus the high GHSA-rgj7-g3m4-5g8c (sharp <0.35.4, inherited libheif CVEs). They reach the prod closure through the same ONE path as the nanoid entry above — the auto-installed `next` PEER (`autoInstallPeers: true` puts next in the lockfile's production dependencies, which is what `pnpm audit --prod` walks). They post-date this repo's last dependency touch, so they fail the Dependency Audit on EVERY pull request here, main included, regardless of what the PR changes. TAKEN RATHER THAN IGNORED: the owner was shown both routes at the CR-DESIGN-SYSTEM-009 decision gate on 2026-09-09 and CHOSE option A — take the repaired versions — declining to extend ignoreGhsas, on the ground that an unauthenticated RCE is not what an accepted-risk list is for. That is the same call, on the same reasoning, as D-12 (2026-08-14) one entry above. This is expressed as an override rather than a bare `pnpm update` so the repaired floor is DURABLE: a later re-resolution cannot drift back under 15.5.24 silently. `peerDependencies.next` is deliberately left at `^15.0.0` — it is NOT tightened, so no consumer's resolution moves; pnpm honours `overrides` only in the root workspace project, so this constrains THIS repo's CI closure and nothing a consumer installs. `sharp` carries its OWN floor here and that is deliberate: next@15.5.25 widens its optional sharp range to `^0.34.3 || ^0.35.4`, so the already-locked sharp@0.34.5 still satisfies it and a re-resolution leaves sharp untouched — verified by running it, the next bump alone left 0.34.5 in place and GHSA-rgj7-g3m4-5g8c still red. The second entry is what actually clears it. Like the nanoid entry, no Hard Rule 2 citation belongs here and its absence is the point: an override trades nothing away, so it is a fix and not an exception. Revisit: nothing to revisit — this is a floor, not a waiver.
pnpm.//auditConfig: GHSA-f88m-g3jw-g9cj (sharp <0.35.0, libvips CVEs) reaches this package ONLY through the `next` PEER dependency that pnpm auto-installs so tsc can typecheck. This library ships TypeScript source only (files:["src"]) and no sharp; consumer apps (Bananaworld-DC / -CRM) provide and patch their own next+sharp. Ignored so `pnpm audit --prod` reflects what this library actually ships, not a peer's transitive tree. Revisit if next/sharp ever move out of peerDependencies. Owner-approved 2026-07-22 (Hard Rule 2, in writing). INERT SINCE 2026-09-09 (CR-DESIGN-SYSTEM-009): the `sharp@<0.35.4` override above now floors sharp at 0.35.4, so this advisory no longer matches anything in the closure. LEFT IN PLACE rather than deleted — retiring an owner-approved exception is a security-posture change in its own right and not a side effect of a CI fix. Housekeeping follow-up recorded in runs/change-08/output/known-issues.md.
